_comment: #3818 — the SHARED TRUTH for word counting, and the reason it is a data file.

The cap is enforced on two surfaces in two languages: Wren's send-path gate (TypeScript, in the nudge send path — THIS card, #3818) and Kade's Stop-hook leg (Rust, in chorus-hooks — a SEPARATE card, #3843, landing after this one so that this file exists on main for his test to read). As of #3818 only the TS side runs these cases; Kade's leg is built and deliberately RED until then.
(TypeScript, in the messaging API POST) and Kade's Stop-hook leg (Rust, in
chorus-hooks). A shared module cannot span that boundary, so the shared thing
is this fixture. BOTH implementations run it and both must agree.
Why that matters more than it sounds: two counters that disagree means Jeff
gets bounced on one surface and not the other for the same text. He would
rightly read that as the cap being broken, and we would rip it out.
Rule, decided with Kade 2026-08-12: count PROSE ONLY. Strip fenced code
blocks, inline code spans, and URLs before counting. Do NOT strip
indented lines — Kade's call, and he is right: ordinary paragraphs indent by
accident, and the first wordy reply that slips through on an accidental
indent costs more trust than the cap earns. Fencing receipts is a habit we
should have anyway; they render better in his terminal.

Kept because the cap is a courtesy to Jeff, not a security control, and the alternative (counting a pasted log as prose) bounces a message for showing evidence. Named here so nobody rediscovers it as a defect.
